TRV.rationale: Travelers delivered an excellent Q1 2026 with net income of $1.71B ($7.78 EPS) vs. $395M ($1.70) a year ago, driven by normalized catastrophe losses ($761M vs. $2.266B) and 9% higher net investment income. Core ROE of 19.7% (trailing 4Q: 22.7%) and underlying combined ratio of 85.3% demonstrate strong underwriting discipline. The company returned $2.2B to shareholders including $2B in buybacks and raised its dividend 14% to $1.25/share (22nd consecutive year of increases). Valuation is attractive: P/E of 8.8x sits at the low end of its 365-day range (8.6-14.9x), well below the ~14x level from a year ago, while P/B of 2.1x is mid-range. The stock has appreciated 10.4% over the past quarter but remains cheap relative to its own history given the earnings power improvement. Key risks include Personal Insurance NWP declining 9% (5% ex-Canada divestiture) and QoQ revenue/EPS softness from the incomplete TTM data prevents full annualization. The near-term catalyst is the Q1 earnings beat and dividend increase just reported (April 16), which should support re-rating given the disconnect between record profitability and historically low P/E. Macro backdrop is neutral-to-mildly-supportive with stable Fed funds at 3.64% and rising 10Y yields supporting investment income.
